content: Do not take valsartan if you are pregnant. If you become pregnant while taking valsartan, contact your doctor immediately, as this medication can harm the fetus. Valsartan is prescribed to treat high blood pressure, either alone or in combination with other medications. It is also used to manage heart failure in patients who cannot tolerate angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors. Valsartan belongs to a class of drugs called angiotensin II receptor antagonists, which work by blocking the action of certain chemicals that tighten blood vessels, allowing blood to flow more easily. Valsartan is available as an oral tablet. For high blood pressure, it is typically taken once daily, with or without food. To ensure consistent use, take it at the same time every day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take valsartan exactly as directed. Do not take more or less than prescribed, and do not take it more frequently than instructed. Your doctor may start you on a low dose and gradually increase it. Valsartan helps control high blood pressure and heart failure but does not cure these conditions. Continue taking valsartan even if you feel well, and do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses. Ask your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before taking valsartan, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to valsartan or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking. Be sure to mention ACE inhibitors (e.g., benazepril, captopril, enalapril, lisinopril), beta blockers (e.g., atenolol, metoprolol, propranolol), and diuretics (water pills). Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you closely for side effects. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had kidney or liver disease. Additionally, let your doctor know if you are planning to become pregnant or are breastfeeding. If your doctor prescribes a low-salt or low-sodium diet, follow these instructions carefully. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Valsartan may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience dizziness, headache, excessive tiredness, diarrhea, stomach pain, back pain, or joint pain, especially if these symptoms are severe or persistent. Some side effects can be serious. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs; hoarseness; difficulty breathing or swallowing; or fainting. If you experience any unusual problems while taking valsartan, inform your doctor. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store valsartan in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication properly. Consult your pharmacist about the correct disposal method. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the person has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911. Symptoms of overdose may include dizziness, fainting, or a rapid or pounding heartbeat. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your blood pressure should be monitored regularly to assess your response to valsartan. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
